claims.text: A small degree of nanoscale chemical heterogeneity promotes localized magneto-structural coupling near the Curie temperature in rare-earth-free HEAs.
Nanoscale clustering enhances spin reorientation and short-range magnetic ordering.
Enhanced spin reorientation and short-range magnetic ordering produce a strong magnetocaloric effect at applied fields below 1 T.
Limiting clustering to the nanoscale prevents the large-scale lattice distortions that would induce hysteresis or compromise mechanical stability.
Conventional casting or homogenization yields a nominally uniform HEA microstructure without intentional nanoscale segregation.
Subsolidus annealing between 800°C and 1100°C for 1–2 hours followed by rapid quenching can subtly modify chemical ordering and enable nanoscale clustering.
The proposed heat treatment can produce nanoscale clustering without detrimental phase segregation.
The relevant structural mediator is nanoscale chemical heterogeneity consisting of small clusters or interfaces within an otherwise compositionally mixed HEA.
Nanoscale chemical clustering enhances localized magneto-structural coupling near the magnetic phase transition.
Localized magneto-structural coupling strengthens the magnetocaloric response by tuning short-range magnetic interactions.
Overall homogeneity arising from high-entropy mixing ensures rapid heat exchange.
Overall homogeneity limits lattice distortions that would otherwise cause hysteresis or weaken mechanical properties.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, enhanced nanoscale heterogeneity will increase the low-field adiabatic temperature change or magnetic entropy change.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, enhanced nanoscale heterogeneity will lower magnetic hysteresis.
Relative to the homogeneous baseline, enhanced nanoscale heterogeneity will preserve or improve mechanical stability.
The proposed mechanism is expected to apply within ±50 K of the Curie temperature and at applied magnetic fields below 1 T.
The proposed mechanism is not expected to apply to binary or ternary alloys or to HEAs with macroscopic phase segregation.
Increasing nanoscale heterogeneity without increasing ΔS or ΔT_ad, or while increasing hysteresis or degrading mechanical stability, would falsify the hypothesis.
